note: Sub-pathauto's entire state is the config object subpathauto.settings with two keys, depth (integer) and redirect_support (boolean), edited at /admin/config/search/subpathauto (route subpathauto.admin_settings, permission 'administer url aliases'). Behaviour comes from one service, path_processor_subpathauto, tagged path_processor_inbound and path_processor_outbound at priority 50. A quirk worth testing: depth 0 means UNLIMITED in code (the form labels it 'Disabled'), while a missing/NULL depth disables processing entirely - which is what the alias-subpath reset exploits so the execution case genuinely fails on empty state. The hard alias case verifies real runtime behaviour by running the live path_processor_manager over /subpathauto-eval/edit rather than just reading config back.

evals.prompt: A Drupal 11 site has node/1 aliased to /about-us, but /about-us/edit returns a 404. The subpathauto contrib module is installed. What does subpathauto do about this, and by what mechanism does it hook into Drupal?
evals.expected_output: Sub-pathauto registers the service path_processor_subpathauto (Drupal\subpathauto\PathProcessor) tagged path_processor_inbound and path_processor_outbound at priority 50. Inbound it strips trailing segments, asks core's path_alias.path_processor whether the shortened parent is an alias, and rebuilds /node/1/edit; outbound it does the reverse so links render as /about-us/edit.

evals.prompt: Which configuration object does the Drupal subpathauto module use, what keys does it contain, and at which admin path is it edited?
evals.expected_output: Config object subpathauto.settings with two keys: depth (integer, maximum number of trailing sub-path segments to try) and redirect_support (boolean, use the Redirect module when resolving). It is edited at /admin/config/search/subpathauto (route subpathauto.admin_settings), which requires the core permission 'administer url aliases'.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal subpathauto module, the 'Maximum depth of sub-paths to alias' select offers 0 labelled 'Disabled'. What does the value 0 actually do inside PathProcessor, and what happens if the depth value is missing entirely?
evals.expected_output: getMaxDepth() returns the raw config value and the loop condition is ($max_depth === 0 || $i < $max_depth), so 0 means no limit at all - every sub-path level is tried, despite the form calling it 'Disabled'. If depth is NULL/absent the strict === 0 check fails and $i < NULL is false, so the loop never runs and no sub-path is ever resolved: that is the real off state.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the subpathauto module is installed and configured. Inspect the running site and tell me the configured maximum sub-path depth, and whether redirect support is switched on.
evals.expected_output: depth is 4 and redirect_support is FALSE - `drush cget subpathauto.settings` shows depth: 4 / redirect_support: false.

evals.prompt: Look at the live subpathauto configuration on this Drupal site. Is its redirect integration currently enabled or disabled, and what is the configured sub-path depth?
evals.expected_output: redirect_support is TRUE (enabled) and depth is 2. `drush cget subpathauto.settings` -> depth: 2, redirect_support: true. The redirect integration only actually engages when the drupal/redirect module is also installed.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the subpathauto module so that it scans a maximum of 3 trailing sub-path segments when resolving an alias, and so that redirects are taken into account when resolving sub aliases. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: subpathauto.settings has depth: 3 and redirect_support: true (set on /admin/config/search/subpathauto, with `drush cset subpathauto.settings depth 3 -y` + `drush cset subpathauto.settings redirect_support 1 -y`, or via the config factory).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a basic page titled 'Subpathauto Eval Page' whose URL alias is /subpathauto-eval. Right now /subpathauto-eval/edit does not work - it is not recognised as the edit form of that page, even though the subpathauto module is installed. Make sub-paths of URL aliases work on this site so that /subpathauto-eval/edit resolves to that node's edit form. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The subpathauto.settings config object is missing its depth value, so PathProcessor's loop never runs. Recreating the config with a depth (e.g. `drush cset subpathauto.settings depth 2 -y`, or saving the form at /admin/config/search/subpathauto) makes the inbound path processor turn /subpathauto-eval/edit into /node/<nid>/edit.
